correctness.rationale: The proof defines all real c>0 and uniform filled-volume moments, reduces fourth-order directional isotropy by sign/permutation symmetry to H(c)=J400-3J220, and evaluates H by exact three-simplex inclusion–exclusion. The projective transform of H on (1,2) has exactly one coefficient sign change and opposite boundary signs, hence exactly one root by Descartes. The transformed H on (2,3) has all negative coefficients, and octahedral/cubic outer regimes have fixed nonzero signs. The sixth-order defect J600-5J420 is strictly negative throughout an exact rational isolating interval for the root, certified by ten negative transformed coefficients. The actual embedded standard-library script regenerates each polynomial from the monomial integral formula, checks all exact coefficients and signs, and isolates the algebraic root; quadrature is only corroborative. No extrapolation from a grid is used.

value.rationale: The vanishing of a fourth-order cubic harmonic is a motivated geometrical moment invariant, not a chosen numerical parameter or routine endpoint table entry. Determining the one nonregular cubically symmetric body with the isotropic fourth moment across an entire octahedron-to-cube truncation path gives a natural complete one-parameter classification, with an exact algebraic parameter, a proof of uniqueness, and a nontrivial sixth-order obstruction. This provides a clean counterexample to confusing finite cubic symmetry with anisotropy at every even order, relevant to geometric moment reconstruction and directional measurements.
